rationale: Retain Hudson Transmission Project as an active Argo-managed transmission investment and retain APG Asset Management as an indirect beneficial co-investor. The project's current owners page identifies Argo as principal investor, while the 2018 New York PSC ownership petition establishes that AMF Oratam Investments LLC was formed to invest in Hudson, that Argo is its managing member, and that APG Infrastructure Pool 2014 participated through wholly owned Sogra Investment Holding B.V. APG's own 2022 periodic disclosure subsequently listed Hudson Transmission Partners as 6% of APG Infrastructure Pool 2014 assets. Lotus reports that its sale to Argo closed in March 2019, and no later Argo or APG disposition, pending sale, or change of control was found through August 8, 2026. Correct both generic vehicle labels, add legal-company aliases and the official website, use the current Fairfield office as headquarters, refresh the concise operating description, replace the quarter-only investment milestone with the disclosed March 2019 close, and attach direct evidence to every milestone. The 37.7% APG interest disclosed for the 2019 closing is not carried into the current stake field because no current percentage has been publicly disclosed. CalSTRS is not added because it is outside the supplied 100-manager census and this task is scoped to the accepted APG and Argo holdings.

beforeImage.name: Hudson Transmission Project
beforeImage.description: Hudson Transmission owns and operates a transmission interconnector linking New Jersey and Manhattan. Its customer base is the regional power market, with capacity contracted to support transfers between PJM and New York City load zones. The project operates a contracted transmission model rather than a traditional rate-regulated utility model. Public materials describe a 660-megawatt underground and underwater link that entered service in 2013 and includes associated transmission upgrades in New Jersey. The asset is strategically positioned to move power into New York City and has historically supported a long-term arrangement with the New York Power Authority. Argo signed to acquire Hudson Transmission in 2018 and public materials describe principal equity ownership as acquired in early 2019 through a managed investment vehicle. Current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

afterImage.name: Hudson Transmission Project
afterImage.description: Hudson Transmission Project is a 660 MW, 7.1-mile high-voltage direct-current merchant transmission link between Ridgefield, New Jersey and Manhattan. Hudson Transmission Partners, LLC owns the project and PowerBridge operates it; 575 MW, or 87.12% of capacity, is contracted to the New York Power Authority through June 2033. The line entered commercial service in June 2013. AMF Oratam Investments LLC, managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, acquired the project's 94% Class C economic interest in March 2019. APG Infrastructure Pool 2014 participates indirectly through Sogra Investment Holding B.V. and disclosed Hudson Transmission Partners as 6% of pool assets for 2022; current beneficial ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.
